title: AI Use Case Design Across Cloud, Data Platform, and IoT Boundaries (2026)

questions.question: Which architecture pattern does the factory-floor use case receive after combining its source boundaries?
options: CLOUD_FIRST_RAG, because the ERP history is in a private cloud
ON_PREMISES_INFERENCE, because latency alone determines the pattern
HYBRID_FEDERATED, because sovereignty, latency, and ownership boundaries are all present
EDGE_PREPROCESSED_RAG, because regulated ERP history removes ownership
questions.explanation: The OT sensor has sovereignty, latency, and ownership boundaries; the regulated ERP source adds sovereignty and ownership. The combined set contains all three, selecting HYBRID_FEDERATED.

questions.question: What pattern does select_pattern choose for the regulatory-document use case with sovereignty and ownership but no latency boundary?
options: CLOUD_FIRST_RAG, because regulatory documents are batch data
EDGE_PREPROCESSED_RAG, because every personal source is streaming
HYBRID_FEDERATED, because ownership always implies an edge model
ON_PREMISES_INFERENCE, because sovereignty without latency selects the on-premises path
questions.explanation: The on-prem personal source creates sovereignty and ownership, but its 86,400-second refresh rate does not create latency. The selection rule maps sovereignty without latency to ON_PREMISES_INFERENCE.

questions.question: Why does the customer-churn workload select CLOUD_FIRST_RAG despite having a latency boundary?
options: It has no sovereignty boundary; ownership and latency alone fall through to CLOUD_FIRST_RAG
Latency boundaries are ignored for all CRM sources
The 60-second refresh rate is too slow to create any boundary, so no pattern is selected
CLOUD_FIRST_RAG is always preferred when two sources are present
questions.explanation: The product-usage stream creates latency and both internal sources create ownership, but neither source is OT/on-prem or personal/regulated. With no sovereignty flag, select_pattern returns CLOUD_FIRST_RAG.

questions.question: Is the factory-floor latency pipeline feasible under its 3,000 ms budget?
options: No; its fixed edge stages alone exceed 3,000 ms
Yes; the 2,480 ms total allocation stays within the budget
No; any LLM inference stage makes an IoT pipeline infeasible
Yes only after removing the OT-to-IT bridge from the calculation
questions.explanation: The six allocations sum to 2,480 ms (500+200+350+80+1200+150), below 3,000 ms. run_latency_model therefore reports the pipeline as within budget.

questions.question: What is the binding constraint for customer-churn prediction when its 6,300 ms allocation exceeds a 5,000 ms budget?
options: Feature retrieval at 400 ms, because it is the first stage
LLM inference at 600 ms, because model calls are always fixed
Streaming event ingestion lag at 4,800 ms, the largest non-negotiable stage
RAG retrieval at 300 ms, because retrieval cannot be negotiated
questions.explanation: The total is 6,300 ms, and the overrun branch chooses the largest stage marked non-negotiable. Streaming event ingestion is fixed at 4,800 ms, so it is the binding constraint.

questions.question: What pattern does a regulated on-prem source with a 3,600-second refresh rate receive by itself?
options: HYBRID_FEDERATED, because every regulated source is also streaming
EDGE_PREPROCESSED_RAG, because on-prem always implies a latency boundary
CLOUD_FIRST_RAG, because ownership has no architectural consequence
ON_PREMISES_INFERENCE, because regulated sensitivity creates sovereignty without latency
questions.explanation: Regulated sensitivity adds sovereignty and non-public data adds ownership. A 3,600-second refresh is not below the one-second latency threshold, so the on-premises pattern is selected.
